name: AMC Segmented Glass
description: A frosted-glass segmented control for page navigation: a recessed glass tray with a raised glass thumb that sits on the current page and glides to the segment under the pointer or keyboard focus, driven by CSS :has() alone.
useFor: Two to eight sibling pages or views on a List region: switching a page between Board, List and Calendar views, or between Orders, Invoices and Customers. One level; sub entries are ignored.
helpText: List template for view switching and page-level navigation. Each entry is a real link with icon and label; the current entry gets aria-current=page. Segments share one width, and a raised glass thumb marks the current page and slides to the hovered or keyboard-focused segment without JavaScript. Lists longer than eight entries, and browsers without :has(), keep a static glass thumb on the current segment. The control scrolls horizontally when it is wider than its container. Template options: Icon only hides the labels visually, keeps them for screen readers and shows them as a tooltip on hover and focus; Stacked puts the icon above the label; Primary thumb fills the thumb with the primary color; Stretch spans the full width; Large raises the height. Under prefers-reduced-motion the thumb jumps without sliding; in forced-colors mode the current segment gets a system outline.

templateOptions.name: Icon only
templateOptions.help: Shows only icons; the label stays available to screen readers and appears as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Every entry needs an icon.

templateOptions.name: Stacked icon and label
templateOptions.help: Places the icon above a smaller label, like an app tab bar.

templateOptions.name: Primary thumb
templateOptions.help: The glass thumb takes the primary color and the segment on it switches to the primary contrast color.

templateOptions.name: Stretch
templateOptions.help: The control spans the full width of the region with equal segments.

templateOptions.name: Large
templateOptions.help: Taller segments with larger text and icons, for page headers and touch screens.
